series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Bollinger gap expansion after prior trend as rising-vol reversal sensor
mechanism: Require three consecutive expanding upper-lower band gaps (Gap(t)>Gap(t+1)>Gap(t+2)); then read the trend that preceded the expansion (closes falling → long; closes rising → short). Rising band gap is treated as a volatility spike at trend end that often precedes reversal; article notes breakout-continuation risk if volume/bar-range is not contracting.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY daily 2023 (RSI tests); Bollinger patterns carried from prior part
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a concrete vol-regime-change feature: expanding envelope after a directional run, with an explicit prior-trend polarity and a volume/range confirmation gate—not just raw ATR.
quote: the widening of the gap between the upper and lower bands of the Bollinger is always taken as an indication of rising volatility. In the case of this pattern because this volatility rise comes at the end of a trend... a widening gap... after a bullish run is considered a bearish signal while similar widening gaps after a bearish run are indicative of a long signal.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Bollinger band skew/angle asymmetry as breakout-orientation sensor
mechanism: Over last 3 bars, lower band rising faster than upper by ≥ m_deviation×(upper change) → bullish breakout orientation; mirrored falling-upper-faster-than-lower → bearish. Captures asymmetric envelope tilt before price pierces the band.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Wizard EA pattern map tests (Bollinger pattern 7)
why_new_for_mis: Senses directional pressure from relative band slopes rather than mid-band or width alone—useful as a breakout-regime precursor feature.
quote: When the lower band is rising faster than the upper band by a multiple equal to or greater than the Bollinger Band's deviation input parameter, we interpret this as a bullish signal... this sort of setup portends a break-out on the upside.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: RSI failure-swing vs level-occupancy as sharper momentum-change sensor
mechanism: Pattern 0: RSI≤30 long / ≥70 short (level occupancy). Pattern 1: prior bar beyond threshold then current bar back across 30/70 (failure swing). Article argues failure swings confirm sentiment shift without needing price confirmation and are sharper than raw OB/OS.
why_new_for_mis: Separates static excess-state from the crossing event that marks regime change—MIS can emit both a level feature and a swing-event feature.
quote: failure swings... confirm a shift in market sentiment that is confirmed by more than one RSI move. They indicate that sentiment is reversing without necessarily needing price confirmation.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: RSI–price divergence and hidden-divergence continuation sensors
mechanism: Classic: 3-bar price lower lows with RSI higher lows → bullish divergence; price higher highs with RSI lower highs → bearish. Also notes hidden bullish (price HL + RSI LL) and hidden bearish (price LH + RSI HH) as continuation marks. Warns divergence may be pullback not reversal.
why_new_for_mis: Provides both reversal-divergence and hidden continuation features from the same RSI–price coupling—useful regime-change vs trend-persistence discrimination.
quote: a bullish divergence being signalled when price makes lower lows while the RSI is making higher lows... Noteworthy as well are hidden divergences. These serve as postmarks to a trend continuation.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: RSI local peak/trough trendline break over last 5 readings
mechanism: Within last 5 RSI values detect alternating peak sequence; declare bullish if current RSI ≥ extrapolated peak line 2*Base(t+2)-Base(t+4); mirrored for troughs. Does not find true fractals—only recent 5-bar structure.
why_new_for_mis: Lightweight oscillator-structure break sensor without needing chart geometry libraries—good short-horizon momentum-structure feature.
quote: we are not necessarily looking for the last true peaks or troughs of the RSI, but rather are checking to see if in the last 5 RSI readings we have a sequence of peaks... then we simply check for the break of the trend line.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Multi-timeframe RSI concurrent overbought/oversold concurrence
mechanism: Require RSI≤30 (or ≥70) on both chart TF and a larger alternate TF RSI handle before emitting buy/sell. Larger TF filters noise of shorter TF.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY daily 2023 with larger second TF
why_new_for_mis: Cross-horizon concurrence of excess-momentum states as a multi-scale regime feature for MIS.
quote: Our final pattern, pattern 7, simply takes pattern 0... and applies it across multiple time frames... our second time frame will be larger than the default test time frame.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: SAR flip after compression-zone (low mean SAR step) as vol-breakout flip sensor
mechanism: Walk prior SAR side while SAR stays on that side; compute mean |SAR change|/count. Compression if that mean < 0.02×|SAR−price| at flip. Emit only when flip occurs after this compressed prior trend. Prefer low-vol markets for raw gap crossovers; compression refines them.
why_new_for_mis: Quantifies pre-flip SAR step compression as a low-volatility → flip event—explicit vol-regime change feature tied to SAR geometry.
quote: if a step fraction of the initial SAR gap from price, is more than the mean change in the SAR values over the previous trend, then we had a compression.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Accelerating SAR-dot gaps as trend-continuation strength sensor
mechanism: Bullish if successive SAR increments increase for 3 steps while SAR remains below lows; bearish mirrored above highs. Targets cases where initial flip gap was small (laggard continuation).
why_new_for_mis: Senses acceleration of the trail itself (not price) as a continuation-regime strength feature.
quote: a bullish pattern being signified by the widening gap between the SAR dots, while the SAR indicator remains below the low prices.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: SAR one/two-bar flip fake-out as choppy-regime / noise sensor
mechanism: Detect SAR side sequence long→short(1 bar)→long (or reverse); treat brief flip as fake-out and resume prior trend. Linked to sideways, low-vol, or noisy regimes; stronger than single flip.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY daily 2023 (no trades for pattern 3 in window)
why_new_for_mis: Turns aborted SAR flips into an explicit noise/chop regime flag rather than a trade trigger alone.
quote: The common causes of these flip-fake-outs are your usual suspects: choppy/ sideways markets, low volatility, or market noise.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Slope-aligned dual-bound price channel half vs SAR side
mechanism: Over MA-period lookback: estimate close slope; pick two highs and two lows whose connecting slopes best match overall slope; project four lines to current bar; mean of projections = channel mid. Bullish if close in bottom half AND SAR below low; bearish if top half AND SAR above high.
why_new_for_mis: Codeable channel-position sensor that avoids pure fractal dependency and couples location-in-channel with SAR trend side—useful regime geometry feature.
quote: Our bullish signal with pattern 6 is for the price to be in the bottom half of the channel, with the parabolic SAR also indicating a long trend.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Dual-horizon bull/bear/flat state grid as RL environment sensor
mechanism: Build short-horizon and long-horizon close-change vectors; map each to bullish/bearish/flat → 3×3=9 environment states (row,col). Feed state coords to DQN_ONLINE (2-6-3) that outputs Q-vector over buy/sell/hold; DQN_TARGET (next-state inputs) supplies Bellman targets y=r+γ max Q_target; copy online→target every m_target_counts. Parent MLP uses DQN output as custom loss target (LOSS_DQN).
why_new_for_mis: Concrete neural regime sensor: multi-horizon discrete market-state coordinates → action-value vector, with target-net stabilization—directly usable as MIS neural sensing stack.
quote: One coordinate measures the type of trend over the short term, while the other looks at the trend over the long term... The DQN therefore maps future rewards for each possible action across all applicable states with the aid of a neural network.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Gamma-discounted delayed-reward credit for news/position horizons
mechanism: Bellman target uses discount γ so Q-values balance immediate vs long-horizon rewards; article ties this to rate-decision positions that suffer adverse excursion before favorable payoff.
why_new_for_mis: Frames temporal credit (delayed reward) as a sensing design choice for MIS when labeling regime outcomes that resolve over multi-bar horizons.
quote: positions that are opened on major interest rate decisions, do not immediately yield favourable excursions. The adverse excursion periods usually headline these positions, and therefore the ability to have and use signals that take this into account like the DQNs can be an edge.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: SAR flip with contracting bar-range as weak-flip / continuation sensor
mechanism: On SAR side flip, require Range(t)<Range(t+1)<Range(t+2). Contracting range = weak flip → continue prior dominant trend (counter to naive flip). Rising range at SAR pierce would confirm flip (suggested, not coded). Bar-range is forex volume proxy.
why_new_for_mis: Pairs trail-flip events with a vol-contraction filter to classify flip authenticity—continuation vs reversal regime discrimination.
quote: if the Parabolic SAR flips from below the price to above (indicating a sell signal) and this is accompanied by dropping price-bar-range, this can be construed as a weak sell signal and more as a harbinger for a continuation in the previous long trend.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Higher-timeframe SAR alignment as macro-trend filter for lower-TF flips
mechanism: Emit lower-TF SAR flip only if alternate higher-TF SAR agrees (Alt below LowAlt for buys; above HighAlt for sells). Weekly used as alt vs daily chart in tests.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit multi-scale trail-alignment regime gate—filters noise flips against broader trend context.
quote: Higher timeframe SAR helps traders understand the larger market context within which the lower timeframe signals are operating.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: ADX DI+/DI− cross and ADX>25 strong-trend / ADX↓25 weakness sensors
mechanism: Pattern0: DI+ crosses above DI− → buy pressure start; reverse → sell. Pattern1: ADX>25 and DI+>DI− → strong bull regime; ADX>25 and DI−>DI+ → strong bear. Pattern2: ADX crosses below 25 while DI−>DI+ → bullish (bearish momentum fading); mirrored for bearish. ADX itself is direction-neutral strength.
why_new_for_mis: Clean separation of directional pressure (DI cross) from trend-strength regime (ADX level/cross 25)—core MIS regime/change features.
quote: The ADX main buffer measures the strength of the trend rather than its direction... readings above 25 indicating a strong trend, while values below 25 suggest a weak or non-trending market.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: ADX vs its own moving average as trend-strength acceleration sensor
mechanism: Maintain MA of ADX main; bullish when ADX crosses up through its MA while DI+>DI−; bearish when same upcross while DI−>DI+. Strength-acceleration independent of price MA.
why_new_for_mis: Applies crossover logic to the strength series itself—senses acceleration of trend intensity, not price.
quote: when the ADX crosses it in the same way price usually crosses moving average buffers on a price chart, this is often a powerful signal.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Price trend vs falling ADX (≤25) divergence and ATR-quiet→spike breakout
mechanism: Divergence: falling closes + falling ADX ending ≤25 → bullish; rising closes + falling ADX ≤25 → bearish (trend losing strength). Breakout: ATR below its average then ATR rises through average and bar range > ATR, concurrent with ADX cross above 25 and directional close—proxy for consolidation→breakout. Hourly needed for enough breakout samples.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURCHF daily 2022; pattern5 optimized on hourly
why_new_for_mis: Two complementary change sensors: strength-divergence against price, and vol-compression-to-expansion breakout with ADX confirmation.
quote: If the ATR had remained subdued for a reasonable amount of time, and it was less than the recent price bar range, then that could imply a break-out.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: On-policy SARSA Q-map over dual-horizon 9-state grid as live regime→action sensor
mechanism: Same 3×3 bull/flat/bear × short/long environment; SARSA updates Q with actual next action under current ε-greedy policy (on-policy), optionally Markov-weighted. Transition action chosen via memoryless Markov row→best next state→argmax Q. Reward = favorable excursion as % of recent price range. RL is the signal model, not merely MLP loss.
why_new_for_mis: Promotes the dual-horizon discrete regime grid + on-policy Q-map to a first-class online sensing/policy module for MIS, with explicit explore/exploit via epsilon.
quote: these are based on 3 simplified market states of bullishness, bearishness, and whipsaw market. Each of these states is then applied on a short time-frame and long time-frame to create a 3 x 3 matrix which implies 9 possible states.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Richer Q-map state axes catalog (indicators, vol, time, sentiment, portfolio)
mechanism: Article enumerates alternate environment axes beyond price bull/bear/flat: MA short/long relation, RSI OB/OS/transient, BB band position, ATR/stddev vol tiers, equity volume tiers, breakout/H&S patterns, session/open-close/day-of-week, news-sentiment polarity, economic-event states, portfolio exposure/risk/drawdown. Dual-axis Q-map can cross any two.
data_needed: chosen axis series (indicators, calendar, portfolio metrics)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Conceptual; SARSA tests on EURJPY daily 2022
why_new_for_mis: Blueprint for expanding MIS regime state spaces beyond price direction—especially vol, session, and portfolio-context axes.
quote: Additional adjustments can be made to the way we have defined the environment states as well by considering alternative market states such as absolute price levels, indicator values of RSI or Bollinger Bands, and crossing this with alternative timeframes.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Monte-Carlo episode-batched discounted return as noise-robust long-horizon reward sensor
mechanism: Buffer rewards for m_episode_cycles; only when buffer full, form G=Σ γ^k R_k and update Q once (on- or off-policy). Infrequent updates evade short-term market noise that per-step Q-Learning/SARSA absorb. Episode length trades bias vs variance. Separate QL_BUY/QL_SELL maps.
why_new_for_mis: Treats episode length as a sensing hyperparameter that controls how much short-horizon noise enters regime-value estimates—valuable for MIS long-horizon regime scoring.
quote: the infrequent updates Monte Carlo simulations performs, given that they only happen once in an episode, do evade market noise which Q-Learning & SARSA are bound to run into since they execute their updates more frequently.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Ichimoku Kumo thickness and twist as future support/resistance strength and regime-color sensors
mechanism: Cloud = area between Senkou A/B projected +26. Thickness |A−B| rising over ~26 bars with price direction → trend-strength/continuation (pattern7). Twist: SpanA crosses SpanB → bullish/bearish Kumo color change as future-regime flip (pattern3). Thick cloud = stronger S/R; thin = easily broken.
why_new_for_mis: Forward-projected envelope width and color-cross give MIS a built-in future-regime and S/R-strength feature set from one system.
quote: a thicker cloud indicates stronger support/resistance, while a thinner cloud implies it may be easily broken... when Senkou Span A is above Senkou Span B, the cloud is bullish... and when Senkou Span B is above Senkou Span A, the cloud is bearish.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Kumo breakout / bounce / TK-cross-relative-to-cloud ensemble
mechanism: Breakout: close pierces cloud boundary in direction of Span order (pattern2). Bounce: pierce then reclaim cloud as S/R (pattern5). Strong TK cross only when crossover occurs above cloud (bull) or below (bear) (pattern6); inside-cloud crosses weaker. Plus price/Chikou both on same side of cloud (pattern9).
why_new_for_mis: Structured cloud-relative event vocabulary (break, bounce, filtered cross, lag agreement) for multi-buffer regime-change sensing.
quote: The bullish signal for this would be marked if the bullish Tenkan-sen/Kijun-sen crossover occurs above the cloud, which... would indicate a strong buy signal.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Temporal-Difference state-value V(s) plus policy-MLP action head
mechanism: Maintain Q_V matrix of state values updated by TD: V(s)←V(s)+α[r+γV(s′)−V(s)] (on/off policy variants also update Q_SA). Because V has no per-action slots, a 3-9-3 classifier MLP takes (env_row, transition_value=V, env_col) and outputs softmax over buy/hold/sell. Online single-bar forward/backward learning.
why_new_for_mis: Splits regime-value sensing (V) from action selection (policy net)—MIS can publish state-value as a standalone regime score while a small net maps it to actions.
quote: TD focuses more on value-based learning where only state values are leaned and updated while the other two algorithms focus on state-action pairing... the suitable action to be selected next is a function of the current environment state and its Q-Value, only.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Alligator sleep→awaken→eat→satisfied cycle as consolidation/trend phase sensor
mechanism: Sleep: jaws/teeth/lips commingled (Williams: ~70–85% of time). Awaken: lips cross jaws (pattern0) or lines untangle after Range≤Spread sleep (pattern4). Eat: lips>teeth>jaws (bull) or reverse, diverging (pattern1). Satisfied: lines reconverge (profit-take / trend-end). Gator histogram |jaw−teeth| and |teeth−lips| colors track expansion/contraction (pattern2).
why_new_for_mis: Explicit multi-phase market-cycle taxonomy (sleep/awaken/eat/satisfied) grounded in three shifted MAs—strong regime ontology for MIS.
quote: markets tend to trend strongly in any set direction for only about 15 – 30% of the time... When the 3 averages are in a tight range, this is often referred to as the alligator taking a nap.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Alligator Range (max−min of three lines) as volatility / fake-out sensor
mechanism: Range=max(J,T,L)−min(J,T,L). Wide range → high vol / strong justified trend; tight range → consolidation. Fake-out prevention (pattern7): price breaks beyond the stack while Range≤Spread (lines not diverged) → treat as false break and fade. Bonus: waning range with intact price trend can imply exit or reverse.
why_new_for_mis: Uses inter-MA envelope width as a vol proxy and couples it to breakout authenticity—practical liquidity/vol-regime feature without order-book data.
quote: High volatility therefore is when the jaws, teeth, and lips are far apart... Low volatility... when the three SMA buffers are close together, which often signals range bound activity.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: PPO clipped advantage (Q−V) policy as stable explore/exploit action sensor
mechanism: Maintain policy weights per action×state; advantage Â=Q_SA−Q_V; probability ratio r=π_new/π_old SoftMax-normalized; clip r into [1−ε,1+ε]; gradient∝(p_new−p_old)×min(rÂ, r_clipÂ); policy←policy+α·grad. Dual-horizon states via m_scale lag. Suited to high-vol where over-exploitation hurts; sample-efficient on scarce/rare-event tick data.
why_new_for_mis: Advantage and clipped policy ratio give MIS a neural sensing update rule that explicitly balances short-term Q vs long-term V under bounded policy shifts.
quote: This method of quantifying the advantage function does emphasize the dependence or the using of policy-based algorithms and value-based algorithms... Â_t is the advantage estimate at time t, which measures how much better an action is compared to the average action at a given state.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: Awesome Oscillator zero-line, twin-peaks, and saucer momentum-regime sensors
mechanism: AO=SMA5(median)−SMA34(median). Zero cross: AO−→+ bullish momentum regime flip; reverse bearish. Twin peaks: two peaks same side of zero without crossing, second closer to zero, intervening histogram shrinking → reversal. Saucer: above zero, two red then taller green (bull); below zero, two green then taller red (bear).
why_new_for_mis: Compact momentum-regime vocabulary (side of zero, peak structure, color saucer) from one Bill-Williams oscillator—good MIS change/regime features.
quote: Twin Peaks occur when two peaks form on the same side of the zero-line either above for bearish or below for bullish with the second peak being closer to the zero line... the zero-line should not have been breached between the two peaks.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: AO histogram magnitude and zero-bounce as momentum-strength / continuation sensors
mechanism: Pattern8: ≥3 consecutive green (bull) or red (bear) bars with |AO|≥8×spread×point → strong momentum persistence. Pattern6: AO approaches zero from above/below then retreats without crossing → continuation bounce. Pattern4 uses AO side+color to filter MA-breakout authenticity. Color flips (pattern7) = early reversal warning.
why_new_for_mis: Histogram height vs spread normalizes momentum strength across symbols; zero-bounce is a continuation-regime feature distinct from zero-cross change.
quote: smaller bars... suggest a weakening trend and therefore a consolidation period, while a longer, more prominent histogram does suggest strong momentum and a prevalent trend has some staying power.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
idea_name: SAC twin-critic min-Q + entropy-regularized Gaussian actor as stochastic policy sensor
mechanism: Actor outputs μ and log-σ vectors; sample a=μ+σ·z and log-prob via Gaussian; critics take (state,action)→Q; actor loss uses min(Q1,Q2) minus α·logπ (α fixed 0.5 here; auto-tune toward target entropy discussed). Twin critics reduce overestimation. States from H1 vs D1 close-change environment (9-state family). ONNX export for MT5 inference.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 with D1 state leg; train 2023-12→2024-08, forward ~4 months
why_new_for_mis: Adds entropy-aware stochastic action distributions and twin-Q conservatism as neural sensing primitives—better explore/exploit regime adaptation than single-net DQN.
quote: The two critic networks make reward forecasts (Q-Values) when inputted with an action and an environment state, and the minimum of the outputs of these 2 networks is used in modulating the loss function used for training the actor network.
